nodes.description: The defining physiologic lesion of absorptive hypercalciuria is increased intestinal absorption of dietary calcium, which raises the filtered calcium load delivered to the kidney while serum calcium remains normal. Heightened intestinal calcium absorption is one of the key contributors to the pathogenesis of primary hypercalciuria.

nodes.description: Sequence variants in ADCY10 alter the activity of soluble adenylyl cyclase, a cytosolic cyclase that generates cAMP in response to bicarbonate and calcium. The enzyme is expressed in gut, renal, and bone tissue, so its dysregulation is proposed to shift calcium handling toward a hyperabsorptive, hypercalciuric state and to contribute to bone loss.

nodes.description: Thiazide diuretics lower urinary calcium excretion by enhancing distal renal tubular calcium reabsorption and are used to treat the hypercalciuria and prevent recurrent calcium stones. In reported ADCY10 pediatric cases, thiazide therapy normalized urine calcium postoperatively.

evidence.reference_title: Two novel heterozygous ADCY10 variants identified in Chinese pediatric patients with absorptive hypercalciuria: case report and literature review.
